messages.content: write a quiet story with sleeps and slept. do not make it sad.

a child sleeps on the sofa while her father reads near the window. later, she asks whether he finished his book. he says that he read a few pages while she slept. she wants to know what happened in the story, so he talks about a girl who found a garden behind a library. the child asks if there is a garden behind their library too. he says that they can look on their next visit.
what is the difference between sleeps and slept in that story?
sleeps is used at the start to tell what the child is doing in that part. slept is used later when her father talks about the time when she was sleeping.
explain the last part simply.
her father talks about the time when she was sleeping and he was reading. that time is already past when they talk.
make his answer about the book one short sentence.
i read a few pages while you slept.
did he say the whole book was finished?
no. he said that he read a few pages. that is less information than saying he finished the book.
write a small story with buys and pay. it can be about a person getting food for a meal with a friend.

a man buys bread at a shop for a meal with his friend. he also gets milk and fruit. when they meet, his friend asks how much she should pay for her part. he says they can look at the price of each thing together after putting the food on the table. first, they make tea and choose what they want to eat.
say the part about the price in one sentence.
he says they can look at the price of each thing together after putting the food on the table.
does buys tell us that he gets the bread for free?
no. buys is about getting something by giving money for it. getting something for free is different.
did his friend already pay in the story?
not yet. she asked how much she should pay, and he said they could look at that after putting the food on the table.
make the story end without choosing a number.
they look at the price of the food and talk about how to share the cost. when both are happy with the choice, they sit down for their meal.
why did you not say one person must pay everything?
the story did not ask for that. the people can talk about a choice that works for both of them.
i want a story that starts before the sun is up. use rise, but do not make the whole reply an explanation.

a girl gets up early and goes to the window. the house is quiet, and the street is almost empty. she wants to watch the sun rise with her grandfather, but he has not come into the room yet. she takes two chairs to the window and waits. soon, he comes with a blanket over his arm. they sit together without saying much. as the sky changes, she thinks about how much she liked waiting with him.
keep only the last sentence.
as the sky changes, she thinks about how much she liked waiting with him.
why are there two chairs?
she wants a place for herself and a place for her grandfather. the story says she wants to watch with him.
did he bring a blanket for each person?
no. the story says he came with a blanket over his arm. it does not say he brought two.
now let the grandfather tell it in two sentences.
i came into the room and found that she had put two chairs by the window. i sat with her, and we watched the sun rise together.
i turned off the television, but i could still hear people talking. does that mean the television was still on?
not always. the sound could come from people in the room, another room, or another thing playing sound. hearing a voice alone does not tell you that the television is still on.
use just one other possible reason in the answer.
hearing a voice alone does not tell you that the television is still on. someone in another room could be talking.
write a short story where the sound comes from the kitchen.

a boy turned off the television and heard a voice. he looked at the screen, then walked to the kitchen. his mother was talking on the phone. he understood that the voice was hers, rather than a sound from the television.
give that story again with fewer words.
a boy turned off the television but still heard a voice. he went to the kitchen and found his mother talking on the phone. the voice he heard was hers.
did he turn the television on again?
the story does not say that. it only says that he went to the kitchen and found where the voice came from.
my cousin lives in another country. i want to ask about visiting without saying i can come yet.
you could say: i would like to visit you one day. what would be a good time of year to come?
i do not want the question to sound like a plan for this year.
i would like to visit you one day, though i do not have a plan yet. what time of year do you like most there?
ask about the time of year in fewer words.
what time of year do you like most there?
can i say their home must be different in every way because it is in another country?
no. another country gives you a different place, but it does not tell you that every part of life is different. ask about specific things rather than saying you already know.
ask about one specific thing.
what is the area around your home like?
why is that useful?
it gives your cousin room to tell you about their own place, rather than having you choose the answer before asking.
write a story about a nurse reading during a break at a hospital. keep it about the book, not about health.

a nurse sits in a quiet room during a break at the hospital. she opens a book about a small village. another worker asks whether it is for her work. she says no. she chose it because she likes stories about people learning to live together. the other worker asks if he can read it after she finishes. she says yes and writes a note to remember that he wants it.
did he ask to take the book right away?
no. he asked whether he could read it after she finishes. that leaves her time to finish her own reading first.
what is the book about?
it is a story about a small village, with people learning to live together. the story does not give much more detail than that.
add a short made up detail about two people in the book who share a garden.
two people live near the same garden. one likes growing flowers, and the other likes growing vegetables. they talk about using different parts of the garden so both can enjoy it.
does the nurse work in the garden?
no. the garden is part of the book she is reading.
what could the heart of a story mean?
it can mean the idea or feeling that is most important in the story. it does not have to be about a real heart in a body.
give me a short example about a family meal.
a story can happen during a family meal. the most important part might be two people learning to listen to each other, rather than what they eat.
say it in fewer words.
the meal can be where the story happens. learning to listen can be the most important part.
write a story with that idea in four sentences.

a father and daughter sit down for dinner. she wants to tell him about a book, but he keeps talking about work. he stops and asks what she wanted to say. she opens her book, and he listens while she reads the part she likes most.
keep only the last sentence.
she opens her book, and he listens while she reads the part she likes most.
what is the heart of that story?
the father makes room to listen to his daughter. that change between them is the important part.
my friend sent a picture with snow in it. can i say there is snow where they are now?
not from the picture alone. it might be an old picture. ask when the picture was taken if you need to know what the place is like now.
make your answer simple.
an old picture does not tell us what the place is like now. ask when it was taken.
write a message asking when the picture was taken.
when did you take this picture? is there snow there today?
my friend says it was last year. what can i say back?
thank you for the picture. i did not know it was from last year. what is it like there today?
keep only the question from that reply.
what is it like there today?
why ask about today after that answer?
you now know the picture is old. asking about today gives your friend a clear question about what the place is like now.
can someone and somebody be used for the same person?
yes. in many simple sentences, you can use either word without changing who you are talking about. someone is at the door and somebody is at the door can give the same information.
does either word tell us the name of the person?
no. neither word gives a name. the person talking may know who it is or may not know yet.
explain it in fewer words.
neither word gives a name. we need more information to know who it is.
make a short conversation where a child finds out.
somebody is at the door. who is it? i do not know yet. can you look from the window? yes. it is our cousin. then we know who has come.
if i change somebody to someone, does the cousin change?
no. the person at the door is still the cousin in that conversation. the change of word does not add a new person.
write one sentence using someone for the cousin before the child knows.
someone is at the door, but the child does not know who it is yet.
in my story, a child draws a tool that can fix any broken toy. make it clear that it is a made up tool.
a child draws a made up tool. it can fix any broken toy in her story. she puts it next to a toy house in the picture and writes that the house will be whole again by morning.
make that story shorter.
a child draws a made up tool next to a broken toy house. in her story, the tool can fix any toy. by morning, the house will be whole again.
can a real tool always fix any broken toy?
no. that is true only in the story. a real toy may need a different kind of work, and some things cannot be fixed.
say that last reply simply.
no. that is true only in the story. a real toy may need a different kind of work, and some things cannot be fixed.
write a question her brother could ask about the story tool.
what happens if two toys need to be fixed at the same time?
does asking that make the story wrong?
no. it gives the child a new idea to think about inside her made up world.
i like helping my friends, but i find it hard to receive help myself.
is it hard to ask for help, or hard to say yes when someone wants to help you?
ask with fewer words.
is asking hard, or is saying yes hard?
it is hard to say yes. i feel like i should do everything myself.
you can do many things yourself and still have help with one part. having help does not mean you did nothing.
say that with a simple example.
you can carry some books and let a friend carry the rest. you both help, and you still do part of the work.
give me a simple reply to a friend who asks whether i want help carrying books.
yes, thank you. could you carry these two while i carry the rest?
write it without thank you.
yes. could you carry these two while i carry the rest?
tell me a short story with a question at the end, rather than the answer.

a boy finds a small container under his desk. inside is a key and a note with his name on it. he asks his sister whether she left it there, but she says no. when he takes the key to the kitchen, his father puts down his book with a smile. what will he say when the boy asks about the key?
keep only the last two sentences.
when he takes the key to the kitchen, his father puts down his book with a smile. what will he say when the boy asks about the key?
do we know that the father knows it just because he has a smile?
no. a smile alone does not tell us that. the father has not answered yet, so we still do not know what he will say.
keep the story open, but change the father to the mother.
when he takes the key to the kitchen, his mother puts down her book with a smile. what will she say when the boy asks about the key?
now does the story answer that last question?
no. it stops before the mother answers. people can think about what might happen next.
say that last answer in fewer words.
no. the mother has not answered yet.
